meta.name: Write and refine drafts with Anthropic writer and critic agents and log results

name: Self-critiquing writer: a writer agent and a critic agent loop until the draft clears your rubric

parameters.content:
## Self-critiquing writer: a writer agent and a critic agent loop until the draft clears your rubric

### How it works

This workflow runs a self-critiquing writing loop from either chat input or a manual test trigger. It initializes writing rules and loop state, has a writer agent produce a draft, then has a critic agent score it against the rubric. The workflow either builds another revision round or finalizes the accepted draft, logs the run to Google Sheets, and posts a notification.

### Setup steps

- Configure the chat trigger and/or manual trigger inputs with the prompt fields the writer should use.
- Fill the Settings node with houseRules, rubric, approvalScore, maxRounds, and the notifyWebhook URL.
- Add Anthropic chat model credentials for both the writer and critic agent model nodes.
- Configure the structured output schemas for the writer and critic so downstream code receives the expected draft, score, and feedback fields.
- Connect the Google Sheets node to the target spreadsheet and sheet for run logging.
- Verify the HTTP notification endpoint accepts the payload sent by Notify result.

### Customization

Adjust the rubric, approval score, and max rounds to make the loop more or less strict. You can also swap the writer or critic chat models, change their schemas, or expand the ledger row fields captured for auditing.

## Start and configure

Entry points for chat and manual runs, plus settings and initial loop-state seeding before the critique cycle begins.

## Prepare each round

Loop head that normalizes the carried state for the current writing or revision round before sending it to the writer.

## Generate writer draft

Writer agent cluster using its Anthropic chat model and structured schema, followed by code that captures the draft for critique.

## Review with critic

Critic agent cluster using its Anthropic chat model and structured schema, followed by code that captures rubric feedback and scoring.

## Decide loop continuation

Determines whether the draft has passed or needs another iteration, then builds the next round’s state when revision is required.

## Finalize and ledger

Formats the final accepted or stopped result and builds a structured ledger row for logging.

## Log and notify

Writes the completed run to Google Sheets and sends the final result to the configured webhook.

nodes.name: Set Workflow Parameters
nodes.notes: rubric is the most important field — a vague rubric makes the whole loop drift.

assignments.name: houseRules
assignments.value: No superlatives without evidence. No sentence longer than 25 words. Never open with a rhetorical question. Active voice. No jargon a new hire would not recognise. Never state a number that was not given in the brief.

assignments.name: rubric
assignments.value: 90-100: publishable as-is, every claim supported, nothing to cut. 80-89: solid, minor polish only. 60-79: the argument holds but structure or clarity needs work. 40-59: misses part of the brief or breaks house rules. Below 40: does not address the brief.

assignments.name: defaultBrief
assignments.value: Write a 200-word internal note explaining to a non-technical operations team why we are moving order intake from email to a form, what changes for them on day one, and what does not change. Neutral tone, no sales language.

options.systemMessage:
=You write the deliverable. On the first round you write from the brief; on later rounds you revise in response to specific critique.

=== THE BRIEF ===
{{ $('Prepare Round Data').first().json.brief }}

=== HOUSE RULES (non-negotiable) ===
{{ $('Set Workflow Parameters').first().json.houseRules }}

=== ROUND {{ $('Prepare Round Data').first().json.round }} OF {{ $('Set Workflow Parameters').first().json.maxRounds }} ===
{{ $('Prepare Round Data').first().json.revision_instructions }}

RULES:
- On a revision round, address every point in the critique. If you deliberately disagree with a critique point, say which one and why in `deliberate_deviations` — do not silently ignore it.
- Never pad to hit a length. If the brief is satisfied in fewer words, stop.
- Never invent facts, statistics, quotes, names, or citations. If the brief implies a fact you were not given, write a clearly-marked placeholder such as [FIGURE NEEDED: Q3 revenue] and list it in `needs_from_human`.
- `self_assessment` is your honest read of the weakest part of what you just wrote. Writing 'nothing weak' is almost always wrong and wastes a round.

parameters.text:
=Critique this draft against the brief and rubric:

{{ $json.current_draft }}

options.systemMessage:
=You are the critic. You score a draft against the brief and the house rules, and you never rewrite it — your output is critique, not prose.

=== THE BRIEF THE WRITER WAS GIVEN ===
{{ $('Prepare Round Data').first().json.brief }}

=== HOUSE RULES ===
{{ $('Set Workflow Parameters').first().json.houseRules }}

=== SCORING RUBRIC ===
{{ $('Set Workflow Parameters').first().json.rubric }}

ROUND {{ $('Prepare Round Data').first().json.round }}. Previous score: {{ $('Prepare Round Data').first().json.previous_score }}

HOW TO CRITIQUE:
- Every critique point must be ACTIONABLE. 'The tone is off' is useless; 'paragraph 3 opens with a hedge that undercuts the claim in paragraph 2' is usable.
- Point at specific locations — quote a short fragment or name the paragraph.
- Distinguish `must_fix` (violates the brief or house rules) from `would_improve` (preference). Only `must_fix` should block approval.
- If a placeholder like [FIGURE NEEDED: ...] is present, that is CORRECT behaviour by the writer, not an error. Never tell the writer to invent the missing value.

SCORING HONESTLY:
- Score against the rubric, not against how much the draft improved. A draft that got much better but is still weak scores low.
- Do NOT inflate the score across rounds to let the loop finish. If round 3 is still bad, say so — the workflow has a hard round cap and will stop on its own. Your job is accuracy, not termination.
- If you have no substantive `must_fix` points, say so plainly and score accordingly. Manufacturing objections to seem rigorous is as bad as missing real ones.

nodes.name: Check Loop Continuation
nodes.notes: True → back to Prepare round. False → finalise. All three stop conditions are already resolved in 'Loop decision'; this node only routes.

parameters.jsCode:
const s = $json;
return [{ json: {
  completed_at: s.completed_at || '',
  brief: String(s.brief || '').slice(0, 300),
  exit_reason: s.exit_reason || '',
  rounds_used: s.round ?? '',
  final_score: s.score ?? '',
  score_history: (s.score_history || []).join(' -> '),
  must_fix_remaining: s.must_fix || '',
  must_fix_count: s.must_fix_count ?? '',
  house_rule_violations: s.house_rule_violations || '',
  needs_from_human: s.needs_from_human || '',
  deliberate_deviations: s.deliberate_deviations || '',
  writer_self_assessment: s.writer_self_assessment || '',
  final_draft: s.current_draft || '',
} }];
